emergence.disease: Non-dystrophic myotonia and periodic paralysis (SCN4A skeletal-muscle sodium channelopathy: paramyotonia congenita / sodium-channel myotonia / hyperkalaemic and hypokalaemic periodic paralysis)
emergence.summary: A spectrum of dominant skeletal-muscle channelopathies caused by mutations in SCN4A, which encodes NaV1.4, the pore-forming alpha-subunit of the skeletal-muscle voltage-gated sodium channel (chr17q23.3). NaV1.4 normally opens to drive the muscle-fibre action-potential upstroke and then INACTIVATES. The myotonic forms (paramyotonia congenita; sodium-channel myotonia) are GAIN-of-function alleles that impair fast inactivation, leaving a persistent/late sodium current that makes the membrane HYPEREXCITABLE -- the fibre fires repetitively after voluntary contraction (delayed relaxation = myotonia). In hyperkalaemic periodic paralysis the same gain of persistent inward current, under a rising extracellular K+, depolarises the fibre so far that the normal sodium channels inactivate and the membrane becomes INEXCITABLE (flaccid weakness). The kit reads this as the skeletal-muscle membrane-excitability axis driven UP (channel GOF -> the gate fails to stay in the OFF / inactivated basin -> a runaway persistent current). This is the SKELETAL-MUSCLE analogue of LQT3 (SCN5A GOF, cardiac late sodium current): the same biophysical lesion (persistent late INa from impaired inactivation) in a sister sodium-channel gene and a different excitable tissue, and -- remarkably -- corrected by the SAME drug class. Correction is to RESTRAIN the over-active channel: mexiletine, a class-IB sodium-channel blocker, preferentially blocks the persistent late current and is the FIRST and only disease-specific licensed antimyotonic (NaMuscla, EMA-approved 2018 for non-dystrophic myotonia; pivotal phase-III MYOMEX, Statland 2012 JAMA RCT). A second, INDIRECT approved arm exists for the periodic-paralysis variants: the carbonic anhydrase inhibitor dichlorphenamide (Keveyis, FDA-approved 2015 for primary hyperkalaemic and hypokalaemic periodic paralysis) stabilises excitability through metabolic acidosis / potassium handling rather than by acting on NaV1.4. IMPORTANT HONESTY: the corrective DIRECTION (block the excess sodium current) is forced [F]; the realised benefit MAGNITUDE is [O] and GENOTYPE-DEPENDENT (some SCN4A alleles respond well to mexiletine, others poorly, by the biophysics of the specific inactivation defect -- the LQT3 mexiletine-sensitive/insensitive pattern). The same gene's LOSS-of-function alleles cause a DISTINCT disease (a congenital myasthenic / myopathic phenotype) -- a different (mechanism) read not conflated here. The gamma read is of the SCN4A promoter switch STRUCTURE (chr17, gamma 1.5187); the disease lesions are coding (inactivation-impairing missense / in-frame changes), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
emergence.emergent_axis: skeletal-muscle membrane excitability -- the persistent / late sodium current through NaV1.4. NaV1.4 normally inactivates after the upstroke; GOF alleles leave a persistent inward current so the fibre is hyperexcitable (myotonia) or, under high K+, depolarised into inexcitability (periodic paralysis). The kit reads the gate over-staying the conducting state -> a runaway late current (axis UP / restrain). The skeletal-muscle contrast to the LOF channels restored by potentiation (CFTR, K_ATP), and the skeletal twin of the cardiac SCN5A late-INa axis (LQT3)

per_gene.note: SCN4A encodes NaV1.4, the alpha-subunit of the skeletal-muscle voltage-gated sodium channel that drives the muscle action-potential upstroke and then inactivates. Myotonic / periodic-paralysis GOF alleles impair fast inactivation, leaving a persistent late sodium current that renders the fibre hyperexcitable (myotonia) or, with raised K+, paradoxically inexcitable (hyperkalaemic periodic paralysis). chr17q23.3. NCBI official symbol SCN4A. Paramyotonia congenita OMIM 168300; sodium-channel myotonia 608390; hyperkalaemic periodic paralysis 170500. Coding lesions; promoter firewall respected.

levers.push_direction: block the persistent late sodium current through the GOF NaV1.4 channel -> damp the repetitive firing / restore a stable resting potential (bring the over-shooting membrane-excitability axis DOWN toward normal)
levers.agent_class: class-IB sodium-channel blocker (mexiletine -- NaMuscla, the disease-specific licensed antimyotonic)
levers.mechanism_grade: [O] benefit MAGNITUDE (stiffness / attack-rate reduction) not sequence-derived; GENOTYPE-DEPENDENT -- some SCN4A alleles are mexiletine-SENSITIVE, others less so, by the biophysics of the inactivation defect, held [O]; the corrective DIRECTION (reduce the excess sodium current) is forced [F].
levers.src: EMA Namuscla marketing authorisation 2018 (first licensed antimyotonic, non-dystrophic myotonia); Statland 2012 JAMA 308:1357 (mexiletine reduces myotonia, RCT); Vicart 2021 Neuromuscul Disord 31:1124 (MYOMEX phase-III)

levers.push_direction: stabilise muscle-membrane excitability indirectly (metabolic acidosis / potassium handling) -> fewer paralytic attacks in the periodic-paralysis variants -- an INDIRECT lever that does NOT act on NaV1.4 itself
levers.agent_class: carbonic anhydrase inhibitor (dichlorphenamide -- Keveyis, approved for primary periodic paralysis)
levers.mechanism_grade: [O] magnitude not derived; INDIRECT (acts via systemic acid-base / K+ rather than the channel), so the on-target direction is forced [F] but the mechanistic distance to the switch is recorded; magnitude [O].
levers.src: Sansone 2016 Neurology 86:1408 (randomized dichlorphenamide trials in periodic paralysis); Keveyis (dichlorphenamide) FDA approval 2015 (first approved drug for primary hyper-/hypokalaemic periodic paralysis)

falsifiers.claim: SCN4A GOF moves the skeletal-muscle membrane-excitability axis UP (a persistent late sodium current makes the fibre hyperexcitable / abnormally depolarisable)
falsifiers.falsifier: an SCN4A myotonia/paralysis allele that DECREASED the late sodium current or LOWERED membrane excitability would refute the channel-on (axis UP) read
falsifiers.measurable_by: late/persistent INa (patch clamp) and resting-potential / repetitive-firing measurements in SCN4A-mutant muscle fibres or heterologous NaV1.4 expression

falsifiers.claim: RESTRAINING the sodium current (mexiletine) is the CORRECTIVE direction
falsifiers.falsifier: if a sodium-channel blocker WORSENED myotonia / increased attack frequency in NaV1.4-driven disease, the restrain lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: myotonia / paralytic-attack response to mexiletine in SCN4A patients (e.g. the MYOMEX endpoints) or relaxation kinetics in mutant fibres
